[quote=technokratisches_kaiserreich;59954574][spoiler=[b]Operation Seeschlange[/b]]

With the Hydronian, Bobian and Sikirskian fleets massing off the coasts of Nestorstaat, the Reichswehr was watching. 

Hydronia, the Bobians and the Sikirskians had made a fatal mistake. 

Pulling within around 25 kilometres of the coast made them sitting ducks to the vast array of Reichswehr coastal defences. 

However, the Kaiserreich had waited. 

The enemies of the Hochkaiser continued to add to their fatal error as they brought almost nonsensical numbers of aircraft carriers, destroyers and frigates within close range of the entire Reichswehr arsenal. 

Admiral Irkodunsk, Bob City, the Hydronian aircraft carriers could now be hit within almost seconds by the DF-26B. 

Radars marked out the locations and movements of enemy craft as passive sonar marked out the locations of THEP and Sikirskian submarines like Christmas lights. 

But the trap, of THEPs own making, would be sprung once the Hydronians had issued their 10-minute threat. 

Once the threat's time had passed, the Reichswehr would pounce into action. 

Tauschkorper-300 miniature decoys move towards the fleet, their radar signatures mimicking that of aircraft, armed with jamming payloads. 

Their purpose is to draw enemy fire and exhaust the missile defense system of the enemy while scrambling their communications and computer systems. 

At the same time J-16CJs along with their J-15E and EK-18 flight packages would launch massive salvos of REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles towards the fleet. Their LOAL capabilities would be deadly. 

Should enemy radar even turn on for a second to search for incoming missiles, the REG-3000s would lock onto their location. Their light frame and extreme speed would make them extremely hard to intercept as they rocket towards the enemies radars. 

Loitering drones would be used as well. These drones would move in swarms towards the enemy fleet. Completely autonomous with fire and forget capabilities they would be near impossible to jam or use EW against. Once they reached their targets they would dive with their explosive packages onto radars. 

A constant flurry of REG-3000s, jamming, drones and TK-300s would work to drain the enemies missile defences and blind their radars. 

Then the real arsenal would arrive. 

Seeschlange-300s could be launched in the hundreds from Nestorstaat. These supersonic, sea-skimming anti-ship missiles would be near impossible to intercept. Near invisible to radar due to their terrain tracking, they would also be able to maneuver to dodge interceptors while deploying chaff near the ships to confuse enemy radar. 

The chaff, designed by Kaiserreich Maschinenwerke marked a new age in the Kaiserreichs naval capabilities. Designed to mimic the movement of missiles they would make entire clouds of false targets over the ships with the purpose of making the enemy waste precious interceptors and time. 

During the war where the Kaiserreich had forced Sikirsk to withdraw, the Kaiserreich had built up massive arrays of A2/AD capabiltiies. 

Unfortunately for THEP and Sikirsk, the Seeschlange-300s would be the tip of the iceberg. 

Donnerkeil naval strike missiles would arc into the skies. These cheaper and older subsonic cruise missiles, utilizing terrain tracking as well, would purposefully create distractor targets. 

Their purpose is to force THEP and Sikirsk to intercept them and waste their resources. THEP and Sikirsk have a limited supply of interceptorsthey can only utilize what is aboard. The Kaiserreich and allies do not share this issue, Nestorstaat has built up massive supplies of missiles. 

As the massive barrage pours onto the enemy fleet, yet another Kaiserreich card comes into play. 

The DF-26Bs. 

Battle-tested during the earlier conflict, the weapons had proven their worth. 

These carrier killers would target the most valuable enemy capital ships. 

These ballistic missiles would be able to strike the enemy within seconds due to their close proximity to the coast. 

Reentering at mach 8 these weapons would go at extremely fast supersonic speeds, making interception highly improbable. 

However, in the highly improbable scenario that an interceptor would be able to take down such a weapon the DF-26 has multiple cards up its sleeve. 

Due to its MIRV capabilities it is able to split into multiple warheads. This increases the damage it can cause while expanding the number of possible targets. Advanced chaff sprays from it as well, adding to the clouds of chaff above the fleet and further confusing any surviving targeting radar. 

The attack wouldnt let the enemy submarines go either. 

LANCELOT-AR systems had been built specifically to hunt submarines. Passive sonar had painted massive targets on the backs of Bobian, and other submarines. 

Reaching supersonic speeds the missiles after being launched from batteries the missiles would move towards the enemy submarines before deploying multiple torpedoes per missile. These would then hone in on the enemy's submarine and intercept. 

Anti-submarine warfare wouldnt stop at that however. Autonomous submarine systems would be deployed against the enemy subs. These cheap swarms of submarines would be armed with torpedoes. 

Using swarm tactics they would work to overwhelm the enemy with sheer numbers, each autonomous system cheaper to manufacture than the torpedoes used against them. 

The enemy would be forced to deal with smart mines as well. These, laid weeks ago in anticipation of a Sikirskian strike would use acoustic and other signals to detect enemy subs. Laying on the seabed, they would launch torpedoes once they detect an enemy submarine in the vicinity. 

These strikes are carefully planned to maximize penetration. 

The enemies missile and point defense systems(CIWS, C-RAM etc) would be exploited to the maximum. 

Waves would be staggered in 30-60 second intervals so their air defense systems arent allowed to reset. 

The missiles and TK-300s move at different angles and multiple waves to overwhelm systems by forcing them to intercept multiple waves at multiple angles. 

Extremely cheap suicide drones pour out towards the enemy fleet forcing them to burn their ammo. 

THEP and its allies have overplayed their hand. Massive fatal strategic mistakes were made by the combined Hydronian, Bobian and Sikirskian fleets. The Reichswehr isnt afraid to exploit them to inflict massive casualties.[/spoiler]
[nation]Gendarme[/nation]
[nation]Bantarus[/nation][/quote]
[i]
The skies over Nestorstaat were already thick with tension, but as the Reichswehrs defenses came to life, the Jomslandic banner stood firm over the gray waters. From the decks of the SHH Heimaeyja, one of the flagships of the Second Commonwealths naval might, Jarl Svanhild Runarsdottir watched the unfolding operation with a slight smirk.The enemy had moved within range.  And so had they. Arrayed across the coast of Nestorstaat were the combined might of the 6th and 8th Jomslandic Fleets, combat-ready and armed not merely for deterrence but for retribution. Hydronian threats had passed their final warning, and the Commonwealth would not be found wanting. Above the ships, Jomslandic 25x JFH-Velum SFA-23 Orion Maritime Patrol Aircraft circled like ravens over a battlefield, relaying enemy missile trajectories to the entire fleet-wide network. High-atmosphere combat drones, The BD23-HA were already in defensive formation around the Heimaeyja, prepared to intercept hypersonic threats with their own MIRV-capable countermeasures.But it was on land, the coast of Nestorstaat, that Jomslands steel would be felt most viscerally.The Sea Battalion's 20,000 Soldiers had dug in under hardened composite emplacements, shielding mobile surface-to-air missile systems, naval radars, and coast-based cruise missile batteries. 5,000 Jomsvikings , clad in storm-gray armor, now patrolled the coasts and hills, dug into a widespread defense grid. Each man prepared to die on that island, but none intending to. Also moving along the coast are the Úlfhéðnar Special Forces armed with long-range MANPADS, ECM drones, and cutting-edge SIGINT packs. Satellite uplinks streamed data in real-time to command aboard the Heimaeyja, giving Jomslandic naval commanders a full battlefield mosaic. And then, the horizon glimmered. Bright, unnatural, a volley rising from the mainland. The Reichswehrs coastal barrage had begun. TK-300 decoys, REG-3000s, and the first wave of loitering kamikaze drones surged toward the amassed enemy fleet. The Commonwealth fleet shifted seamlessly. The Einherjar-class vessels released their Hvitserk-Class EW drones, forming a mobile jamming web across the fleets perimeter. Hydronian anti-radio seekers would find no target here. Radars went dark, replaced by passive targeting and optical tracking. From the Brimbrjótur-class destroyers, Shieldwall Active Interception Systems began their work. Double-layered intercept protocols, projectile and laser, activated in sequenced defense. Chaff blossoms and directed countermeasures burst from the Rakvélklærnar-class vessels, seeding the sky with false targets and luring missile seekers away. This is Jarl Svanhild aboard the SHH Heimaeyja. All units: Shieldwall Protocol is active. Engage all defensive protocols. Do not fire unless fired upon. But if they dare, make history remember this day. Jomsland had no intention to strike first. But the fleets of Hydronia, Bobia, and Sikirsk had sailed into a trap of their own making. As the Seeschlange-300s thundered from the coast behind them, the Jomslandic fleet held formation, an iron bulwark before the storm. Each vessel ready, each warfighter willing, each radar silent, watching the sky.
[/i]
[nation]United Hydronia[/nation]

[quote=alkiragunya;59926998][sPoiLeR=Chapter 17-Arc of the Prohibited Ritual.]
Eu vi algo ali!
Dulbara disse apontando para um arbusto próximo, Yumdahri revirou os olhos enquanto tomava um gole de seu suco e o respondeu em tom sarcástico 
eu que estou privada de sono e você que está vendo coisas? Impressionante
Eu tô falando sério, parece 
Ele não terminou, quando olharam em frente, lá estava ela, parecia uma mulher, alta, envolvida em um manto de penas negras, uma figura alta e esguia, junto de uma pele escura como breu, possivelmente pintura, em seu rosto, mesmo que pouco visível pela escuridão, parecia ter algo alongando seu nariz em formato de bico, aquilo segurava em suas mãos um cajado com diversas marcas, seus olhos eramvazios.
Vocês quebraram o equilíbrio! Os espíritos wauwari me avisaram, vocês realizaram um ritual proibido, sujaram as areias do deserto com sangue, isso é sacrilégio absoluto!
Ela falou com tom autoritário enquanto batia o cajado contra a areia, espalhando-a pelo ar.
Uma Malingeemasela parece diferente, eles geralmente se vestem de animais ou repetem seus hábitos por poder, ganância, mestre Tjilpi é um dos poucos Malingee realmente bons, mas ela parece.neutra.
Yumdahri notou rapidamente conforme analisava a mulher a sua frente, ela logo se introduziu:
Acertou em cheio , quer aplausos? Eu não estou aqui por vocês, há uma perturbação no dreamtime e soube imediatamente que só poderia ser causada pelo conselho, arrogante de sua parte pensarem que os espíritos não responderão!
Ela falou em tom deveras sarcástico, e então ajustou seu cajado para dias costas, e então apontou para Dulbara com seu cajado e então ordenou como se fosse absoluta autoridade:
Não desejo lutar com vocês, apenas me mostrem ontem está o catalisador do desequilíbrio, e o causador.
Dulbara cerrou os punhos, e a desafiou:
Jamais trairemos nossos colegas, eu jamais trairia Kambilla nem ninguém do conselho, de quer mesmo chegar até ele e o totem, passe por mim primeiro!
Ele desafiou indo para cima dela, mas então Yumdahri o puxou pelo braço:
Não vá, você está em estado debilitante demais!
Ela sussurrou, com certa preocupação por Dulbara em sua voz, ele a respondeu com uma voz tentando a acalmar:
Não vou permitir que passe por mim sem lutar, minha lealdade ao conselho não me permite!
Teimoso
Yumdahri revirou os olhos e tomou outro gole de sua bebida, Dulbara sorriu ao sentir o braço dela o soltando, ele então sorriu e avançou contra a Malingee, e berrou Punhos de fogo!
Assim acendendo seus punhos em labaredas ardentes, e então a lançou um combo de socos, a Malingee os bloqueou com seu cajado e então recuou para trás, tirando de seu manto, várias penas negras:
domínio de plumas : PENACHO!
Ela controlou a sua frente fazendo as penas  negras criarem um escudo a sua frente que a bloqueou do combo de socos.
Ele é intenso, mas lento, talvez por estar ferido.
Ela pensou consigo mesma, mas então Dulbara saltou, invocou diversas bolas de fogo ao seu redor, e as lançou contra ela dizendo :
Barragem do fogo eterno!
A resposta imediata da mulher corvo foi de guardar as penas em seu manto e tocou na ponta de seu cajado com o indicador e dedo médio.
Armamento: lança de penas!
As plumas envolveram o cajado, criando uma ponta afiada feita pelas mesmas, ela então começou a se defender cortando as bolas de fogo que eram jogadas com intensidade contra ela, Dulbara voltou ao chão, segurou seu peito, sentia sangue saindo novamente Yumdahri soltou seu copo, o qual derramou o líquido marrom na areia, enquanto ela puxou Dulbara para longe, sabia escolha, já que a Malingee havia atacado com sua lança que pegou centímetros de diferença do rosto de Dulbara.
A Malingee saltou para frente dos dois, e encarou os olhos de Yumdahri, Dulbara já desacordado em seus braços.

"But what price must be paid?"
Tjarrampa raised the first question, and Balunji responded immediately, with a tone of urgency:
"Blood for blood, soul for soul, seems a fair trade, doesn't it?"
"The sacrifice, however, was essential to revive a clan. If an ancient being refuses to acknowledge it..."
Kaltimaka, of the hawk clan (Penguji), raised a question, but was quickly cut off by the master of the waves:
"NEVER dare question Wonambi. The serpent knows more than any mortal. His word is law, even for all in the deep Dreamtime!" He then took the orb in his hands and opened it, revealing it to be hollow. He immediately realized:
"This is a trapping churinga... made to imprison things... from objects to magic or beings..."
The eyes of the other council members widened in surprise at the revelation. Before anyone could say anything, Kambilla entered. He was weak and staggering. If it weren't for Unbaranga carrying him, he might not even have been able to reach it. Kambilla leaned against one of the branches that supported the gunya, and then spoke in a trembling voice, as if he were forcing his own throat:
"I will do it..."
Balunji quickly shook his head, slicing the air in front of him.
"NO! Even with a possible catastrophe, I will not allow the killing of a councilor, not even if he volunteers, especially one who has just rebuilt his clan!"
"Desperate situations...*cough...call for desperate decisions!"
Kambilla countered, balancing on the branch beside her. Balunji, however, remained firm in his decision:
"And do you really think Wonambi demands martyrs? She can punish us for desecrating sacred ground with a forbidden ritual, but it would be an even greater sacrilege to offer the lives of her creations in exchange for sparing us. It's a mockery of the ancestors!"
"So what shall we do?!"
Kialja asked, already somewhat flustered by indecision. Adjusting her feathered cloak, fingering the colorful plumes with subtle vanity as she placed her delicate hands subtly in front of her, Mardu walked through the entrance, accompanying old Ngayhl. The latter then spoke first, bursting between the two with a simple gesture of his fan, causing Kambilla and Balunji to retreat. "Indeed, Wonambi is wise enough to know that the ritual was used for good purposes, not evil like what the Purinina did. Intention changes everything."
He spoke as he adjusted the fan covering his shoulder. Ngayhl, at his side, finally began to say:
"The Purinina were the ones who truly desecrated the temple; Karnagha did it!"
"THEN LET'S KILL HER!"
Tjarrampa said, clenching his fist with enthusiasm. He seemed somewhat excited. They would finally pay "blood with blood" after all, and this encouraged him. But that feeling was soon cut short by Ngarrajin entering. Ngayhl continued. Those present were surprised by his entrance as he stated:
"This would be revenge, not judgment."
His words were sharp as a knife and cold as ice, but he didn't finish. He took some time to himself, adjusting the fiber bracelets on his wrist, and then continued:
"This orb must imprison whoever caused it. Tjuwungu performed the ritual, but the one who brought it to Towurunga was...Balunji!"
Rajin pointed at the First Among Equals, his voice, however, not accusatory, but direct. Balunji fell silent, a frightening lack of sound filling the Council, it seemed...deafening.
"Eh, that makes sense...but...there must be another way, right?" Balunji's voice was trembling. He didn't want to do it, but deep down, he knew it was the only option. There was no other choice. He would have to pay a price to Wonambi, just as Kambilla did... and the price would be a part of his spirit being imprisoned in the orb. He finally gathered the courage to answer:
"But... but, there must be another way, right?"
Ngayhl, however, immediately denied it:
"There isn't. Only then can we calm Wonambi and stop her from punishing Towurunga and perhaps all of Alkiragunya!"
Balunji took a deep breath, then began to think:
"If I do this, I'll surrender a part of my power... Wonambi will be satisfied, but what about the council? How will they be? Desperate situations call for desperate measures, but how?! Maybe, maybe I really have no choice but this..." Finally, after what seemed like an eternity of thought, he answered the guardians:
"Very well... I will do it..."
Balunji was very reluctant, but finally agreed. It was the best thing to do anyway. He looked at the pulsating orb in his hand; his pulse seemed to have slowed. Ngayhl and Mardu smiled at the answer, satisfied. They then walked to the koala guardian's Gunya. Ngayhl crossed his legs and sat on the sandy ground. The sand felt as if it were gently prickling his legs and feet. He finally placed the eucalyptus leaf around his neck on the ground and gestured with his hands. But before he finished, he asked Balunji and Mardu to leave.
There are things that were not meant to be seen, communication with ancestors, is something I do not recommend to you if you want to stay sane. Both were surprised by the request, and then they left the branch tent, each going to a different spot. Balunji leaned against a binirri (bloodwood) tree. He was surprised to see Bedda, the power of the Nalangak, emerge from the dunes like an agile lizard. She made him a proposal:
"Master of the Waves, as you must know... my clan has long fought to enter the council. I have done much to make this happen... and now, we have three councilors hospitalized, and one weakened... I imagine, perhaps in this time of crisis, it would be wise to appoint a replacement..."
She then took Balunji by the shoulders, as if making a more urgent request, but not quite holding on tightly:
"I only ask that you put me on the council. The Nalangak are powerful and influential, and now in times of crisis, I only ask that..." Balunji didn't let her finish, simply removing Bedda's hands from his shoulder, as if pushing away her touch. He then looked into her somewhat tired eyes and said:
"I'll look at your situation later. We're... in a difficult situation, and the council will decide whether this will go ahead or not. I'll give you the answer soon..."
Bedda smiled in response, not a smile of gratitude, but of satisfaction. Now she would finally have the position she so desired, but she was still uncertain. She'd done it several times before, but the council had denied her, but now maybe it would work. It  [b]HAS[/b] to work.
